_meta.description: Business activity catalog. Each entry maps a common activity type to its licensing constraints. This drives the DETERMINISTIC eligibility engine. Edit this file to change rules; do not hardcode activity logic in application code.
_meta.disclaimer: Directional guidance only. UAE licensing categories are granular (thousands of DED/free-zone activity codes). These are simplified buckets for MVP triage. Confirm the exact activity code and its rules with the relevant authority or a licensed corporate services provider.

field_docs.mainland_required: true = this activity generally cannot be conducted for the UAE local market from a free zone and needs a mainland (DED) licence or a mainland branch.
field_docs.free_zone_eligible: true = a free zone licence can be issued for this activity (typically for international / B2B / non-local-market operations).
field_docs.serves_local_market_directly: true = the business model inherently requires selling/serving the UAE onshore public directly (storefront, local clients, physical services on mainland).
field_docs.regulated: true = a sector-specific regulator (e.g. DHA/MOH, RERA, Central Bank, DFSA/FSRA) must license the activity in addition to the trade licence.
field_docs.categories: Tags used to match against free-zone specializations.

activities.label: General Trading (import / export / distribution)
activities.notes: Free zone general trading is ideal for international import/export and re-export. Selling directly into the UAE mainland market requires a mainland distributor/agent or a dual (mainland) licence, because free zone companies cannot invoice onshore customers directly.
activities.source: UAE Ministry of Economy / free zone authority general trading licence guidance

activities.label: Commodities Trading (gold, diamonds, metals, tea, coffee, agri)
activities.notes: Commodities trading is strongly associated with DMCC, which provides commodity-specific infrastructure (vaults, exchanges, DMCC Tradeflow).

activities.label: IT / Software Development / SaaS
activities.notes: Fully free-zone eligible. Tech clusters (Dubai Internet City) add ecosystem value; low-cost zones work fine for bootstrapped software teams.

activities.label: E-commerce (online retail / marketplace)
activities.notes: E-commerce can be free-zone licensed. To hold local stock and deliver to UAE customers at scale, most operators pair the free zone company with local fulfilment/logistics or a mainland presence. Cross-border / dropshipping models fit free zones cleanly.

activities.label: Management / Professional Consulting
activities.notes: Consultancy is one of the most flexible licence types. Free zone consultancies can serve international and (in practice, project-based) UAE clients; ongoing onshore commercial activity may require a mainland licence.
activities.source: DED professional licence / free zone consultancy guidance

activities.label: Media / Advertising / Marketing / Content
activities.notes: Media and marketing are well served by media-focused free zones (SHAMS, Dubai Media City). Certain media/publishing content is subject to UAE Media Council content rules.
activities.source: Sharjah Media City (SHAMS) / Dubai Media City guidance

activities.label: Freelancer (designer, writer, developer, consultant)
activities.notes: Free zone freelance permits are the cheapest legal route for solo operators. Typically limited to a single named permit-holder and a defined activity, with limited or no separate visa allocation on the base package.
activities.source: SHAMS / IFZA / RAKEZ freelance permit guidance

activities.label: Financial Services (asset management, brokerage, fintech, advisory)
activities.notes: Regulated activity. Financial services cluster in DIFC (DFSA) and ADGM (FSRA), which operate independent common-law frameworks. Onshore financial services fall under the UAE Central Bank / SCA. Regulatory approval is separate from and additional to the trade licence.
activities.source: DIFC / DFSA and ADGM / FSRA regulatory frameworks

activities.label: Light Manufacturing / Assembly / Production
activities.notes: Industrial free zones (RAKEZ, Dubai South, KIZAD) provide warehousing and industrial land at lower cost. Selling finished goods into the UAE mainland market still requires a distributor or mainland channel.
activities.source: RAKEZ industrial / Dubai South logistics guidance

activities.label: Logistics / Freight / Warehousing
activities.notes: Airport- and port-adjacent free zones (DAFZA, Dubai South) are purpose-built for logistics. Last-mile domestic distribution into the mainland typically needs mainland transport permits or a local partner.

activities.label: Training / Education Services (non-academic)
activities.notes: Corporate training and professional development can be free-zone licensed. Formal academic institutions and accredited schools require sector regulator approval (KHDA in Dubai) and are often mainland/regulated.
activities.source: KHDA / free zone training licence guidance

activities.label: Retail Shop (physical storefront to UAE public)
activities.notes: A physical shop selling directly to the UAE public must be on the mainland (DED licence) or inside a designated retail/mall environment. Free zones cannot open a general onshore retail storefront for walk-in local customers.

activities.label: Restaurant / Cafe / Food & Beverage
activities.notes: F&B outlets serving the public need a mainland trade licence plus food-safety and municipality approvals. (Food kiosks inside a specific free zone community are the narrow exception and out of MVP scope.)
activities.source: DED / Dubai Municipality food establishment licensing

activities.label: Real Estate Brokerage / Property Services
activities.notes: Brokering UAE onshore property is a mainland activity requiring DED licensing and RERA registration (in Dubai). Free zones cannot license onshore real estate brokerage.
activities.source: Dubai Land Department / RERA broker registration

activities.label: Construction / Contracting / Fit-out
activities.notes: On-site construction and contracting on the mainland require a mainland licence plus municipality/civil-defence approvals and contractor classification. Free zone licences do not authorise onshore construction work.
activities.source: DED contracting licence / Dubai Municipality classification

activities.label: Healthcare Clinic / Medical Services
activities.notes: Clinics treating the public need health-regulator licensing (DHA in Dubai, DoH in Abu Dhabi, MOHAP federally). A dedicated healthcare free zone (Dubai Healthcare City) exists but is outside the MVP free-zone set, so this engine routes healthcare to mainland/regulated.

activities.label: Legal Services / Law Firm
activities.notes: Litigation and advocacy before UAE onshore courts require a mainland licence and bar admission. Legal CONSULTANCY (non-advocacy) can be licensed in DIFC/ADGM under their own frameworks, but general legal practice for the onshore market is mainland.
activities.source: Ministry of Justice / DIFC & ADGM legal frameworks
